findings: case-law-research-platform / CourtListener: the captured repository metadata and README establish a searchable archive of court opinions, but they do not establish citation relationships between decisions (the precedent graph), one of the three defining structures; add an official source documenting citation/reception links or narrow the match to opinion retrieval/search.
non_blocking_notes: Most open-source leaf_matches use the same generic reason text; more specific source-to-core mapping would improve auditability.
OpenHands' README frames the product as an agent control center/orchestration layer; its fit for the autonomous code-editing core is supported mainly by project/workspace and code-review references.
Papermark's README focuses on DocSend-style sharing; its data-room positioning is supported mainly by repository metadata.
CourtListener's README is largely project navigation/ASCII art, so citation-graph support is not captured in the snapshot.
Commercial entries rely on homepage metadata only, which is acceptable for basic authenticity but leaves core workflows at product-marketing level.
Several matches are archived or discontinued projects (Brackets, Sourcetrail, OpenSTF) but remain valid open-source matches.
